Lazy copy-back (VICTORY_LAZY_BACK=1, off by default): what shaders wrote to a copy in the PC's memory is owed to title memory instead of compared and merged after every submission; the pages are made inaccessible and the first touch of a 64 KiB chunk by any thread merges that chunk and gives the page back. Owed chunks are given back before a new snapshot of the range, before the title-memory merge under writes and before kernel writes; views of physical pages are merged at once. Per-frame counts on the copy line; tests fault real memory from other threads.

Textures picked by index: a write the guards do not see landing in an uploaded texture's memory has the slot looked at against the fingerprint of its upload, also after its rechecks ended (settled slots keep it); changes found that way count as told and stop showing as 'nothing to tell of it' (VICTORY_PAGE_RECHECK=0: as before)

Lazy copy-back: a fault on a chunk not owed is taken only when the faulting access would now succeed (a write to read-only memory or a guard stays with the other handlers; the crate's guard tests hung on it)

Lazy copy-back for copies in the card's memory (relay landing): the pieces a flight's compare flags are owed instead of fetched; the first touch fetches that piece alone with a list, fence and buffer of its own, waits for that fetch only, and merges it as the landing does. The fetch runs while the pages are still closed (Source::prepare), the merge only after they open, so a touch from another thread meanwhile waits; the merge itself still runs with the pages open (private memory has no second mapping and the kernel's writes fail on closed pages). WARP test: a touch fetches only its piece from a card buffer.

Fresh tables with constant buffers made from a stamp: the table's other views are made once per list in CPU-only slots and copied with one call, only the constant buffers made per draw (VICTORY_TABLE_STAMPS=0: as before). Sanitise the repository: generic project identity, no title/studio/publisher/console references  In response to the IP enforcement notice against the project network this repository descends from, the repository is rewritten so that it identifies neither the title, the publisher, the console program codename, nor the original upstream project, and so that nothing in it reads as an invitation to use unauthorised files.  * Project identity: every project identifier is now Palmetto - the executable (palmetto.exe), the CMake targets and cache   variables (PALMETTO_*), the runtime's hook prefix (palmetto_*), helpers, tests and docs. File names that carried the old   name were renamed with git mv. * Title, studio, publisher and console-codename references are replaced with neutral wording ("the target title", "the   target console", "the target package", "the publisher"); the local package path example no longer names a drive or a   release group. * The README is rewritten: it describes a clean-room compatibility runtime, states that the repository ships no game, no   keys and no executable, that nothing decrypts content or works around protection, that the user needs their own   legally acquired copy, and that nothing generated from it may be shared. The upstream-project lineage, the original   project's name and link, and the trademark sentence naming the title are removed. * The archive tooling is genericised (ARCH/ARC9 names for the container tools, tests and the hex-pattern file) and the   third-party archive-explorer submodule pointer is removed; the credits keep the public dependencies. * The progress tracker is regenerated from the current measured state: the title boots past 300 s, executes its draws   with 0 refused submissions, presents 33,275 frames to the runtime's own window, and the presented frame is still black   with the measured remaining gaps recorded (texture data path, streamed-block consumer).  Build verified after the rename: PALMETTO_OK; tests built and passing (proxy mock, unimplemented policy, presentation, graphics record, graphics pipeline, XG layout).  No game data, no keys, no executable, no package paths.

frame capture: the cull axis is closed, the constants are sane, and the sampled textures are empty  Two more falsifier boots on the frame-content frontier, both diagnostic-only (default path byte-identical; the pipeline build now uses the recipe's own stage list on the default path, so cache keys and pipeline bytes are untouched):  * PS-only control with culling forced off (the title's vertex stage and pipeline state, the project's constant-output pixel   shader): the presented resource still reads back uniformly black (mean 0, 0 of 16,384 non-black, write control valid),   while the project's own full-screen triangle into the same target reads back its exact colour. The documented-default   back-face culling - the stand-in for the still-undecoded fixed-function state record - is therefore not what discards   the title's fragments. * Constants and centre window: the vertex shader's constants block (V# at the rebased arena address, 0x1E0 bytes) reads   back plausible - mean 17, 78 of 480 non-black, first dwords 3f800000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 3f800000 ...   (a transform-matrix start, not zeros or garbage). The presented resource is black at its centre as well as its origin,   so this is not a corner artefact. frame capture: watch the sampled 4K texture's pages and allow a bounded import-size override  The texture-source increment showed the sampled 4K texture is a placed population nothing writes - but that conclusion came from one window. This adds the diagnostic that tests it over time, opt-in and default-path-identical:  * PALMETTO_TEXTURE_PAGE_WATCH=1 watches up to four placed title-VA spans (every placed texture whose first subresource is at   least 16 MiB, from its creation, plus the armed draw's own sampled texture when its T# resolves). Every 64th submission it   samples non-zero bytes in the page heads (first 4096 B of each 64 KiB page, bounded) and prints the first sample and   every change, so a span that never changes is explicitly measurable rather than assumed. * PALMETTO_TEXTURE_IMPORT_MAX=<bytes> lifts the placed-texture import's 16 MiB cap for the measurement, loudly logged, so   the sampled 33 MB texture can exercise the import path (copy or recorded give-up with its resource id and title VA).   The default cap stays 16 MiB. * The CPU page-read trapping limit is documented honestly in docs/texture_source.md: plain title-side loads cannot be   trapped without changing page protections; the write watch, the device read entry points (ReadFromSubresource/Map were   zero in every boot) and the draw's own sampling stand in. xg: decode the resource-layout record, make the linear layout the default, keep tiling refused  Console texture-layout slot 2 is GetResourceLayout with a 0x1B40-byte record, not the 0x6C8 previously assumed: a 0x18-byte header followed by four 0x6C8-byte planes (each 0x38 + 15 mips of 0x70). The offsets the title itself reads were pinned from both call sites, and the two records the title asks for (2048x2048 and 1024x1024 single-level R8) are filled exactly, with every non-field byte zeroed so no stack bytes survive. Slot 10 is GetResourceTiling (the seven-argument shape, 12-byte subresource entries); it stays refused with the field named, because a tile list only exists for a 64 KiB tiled resource and the window creates none - filling tile indices would be fabricated.  The linear layout is now the default path: the suggestion and texture-computer creation answer only for descriptions whose record can be written honestly (single level, single slice, 1D/2D, single sample, no render-target/depth flags, whole-byte single-plane format), and refuse by name for everything else (buffers, 3D, multiple mips/slices, MSAA, render-target/depth-stencil, planar formats). The measured A/B: 15/8 suggests/creations and zero copies in the old refusal path versus 44/24 suggestions/creations, two filled records and 65 copies / 34,044 B in the default path; both boots ALIVE with no exception, device loss or TDR, and the frame stays black (the content frontier is separate).  port/test/xg_xs_test.cpp grew to 86 checks (and 16 in the refusal arm); both gates green.

The per-object motion reads last frame's object and bone blocks from last frame's uniform snapshot, kept one more frame, instead of having every snapshot copy both neighbours of each such block: the town's snapshot was 2836 KiB a submission with the neighbours and 1916 KiB without, and each byte is copied twice with the motion on (into host memory for the CPU's reads, then into the device copy). vk_mvprev_find still picks the address; the block's bytes and the motion draw's descriptor come from vk_usnap_prev. A block bound at the same address both frames keeps this frame's copy, as before.

With the per-object motion on, the uniform snapshot copies into host memory only the regions the CPU reads back (those holding a vertex-stage block of a bank the motion compares, or of the camera, c4) and writes the rest straight into the device copy, as with the motion off; before, the whole snapshot went through host memory, every byte copied twice. A host region is still copied into host memory first and from there into the device copy, so both hold the same bytes while the game writes guest memory. vk_usnap_bytes reads a host region's host copy and any other from the device copy (slow through the BAR, which only rare readers reach: the merged uniform updates and the test surveys), so every reader gets the bytes it got before. The last-frame copy (vk_usnap_prev) takes host regions only. The snapshot summary gives the bytes copied into host memory.

tools/shader-cache/ard_index.py: rebuild a bf2.ard file index by scanning for the record magic. The records are scattered, so walking cannot work; a 10.2 GB archive scans in 6 s and reproduces the historical 52,409-record index exactly, with every sampled record inflating to its declared size

tools/shader-cache: pack.py, and build_cache.py can now run the whole chain with one command. Two real bugs found by the verification: the default results.tsv header lacked the resources column the runtime searches for by name (every shader would have lost its descriptor bindings and the scene would render flat), and rows were installed for blocks that produced no .spv. Clean room, empty cache: 4.7 min, 12,104 shaders, 12,104 rows, 53.9 MB pack, exit 0, and 50 of 50 sampled .spv byte-identical to a hand-built cache

gfx: put the depth-stencil attachment in GENERAL when a pass samples the depth and writes the stencil in the same draw. Keeping it read-write was right (a read-only attachment zeroes the stencil write mask and the class mask goes black), but the sampler then named DEPTH_STENCIL_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL while the attachment was DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, which is VUID-vkCmdDrawIndexed-imageLayout-00344. GENERAL is the only layout valid for both uses. Verified: the VUID is gone, the picture is unchanged, 2967 frames with no crash

tools/shader: patch_ds_samplers.py, so the stencil-plane fix reaches players. The console lets a float sampler read a depth-stencil stencil plane and the byte lands in the float register unchanged; Vulkan cannot express that, and an S8_UINT view against a float sampler is VUID-vkCmdDrawIndexed-format-07753 (AMD tolerates it, NVIDIA does not). Declaring the sampler uint and bitcasting back is equivalent, and doing it as a rewrite of the player own cache keeps the project free of game data. Validated against four hand-built patches: same VUID gone, no load complaints. Also stops xc2/game/shader-patch from being stageable: a patched shader is a derivative work, which the pre-commit hook already said and the gitignore contradicted

tools/run: report.ps1, one run with every diagnostic on, packed into a zip a stranger can attach to an issue. A rendering bug report is worth nothing as prose - the four facts that decide a diagnosis are the validation layer VUIDs, the capability lines, whether the device was lost, and the frame times. ffhome sent eight logs today and I grepped them by hand; this does it in one step. Never stops the game, packages whatever the run produced including a crash, and -FromLog re-packs an old run

launcher: 60 fps is the default. FPS=60 makes the game step its own 60 Hz loop and HZ=60 sets the present interval to match, so the pacing comes from the game rather than from a host timer at half the rate; -30 still gives the console step

run: fill the shader cache when the game exits, so the next launch is complete. The launcher now turns on dump_missing and ds_debug, and after the game closes fill-cache translates every block the run could not find and retypes the samplers it reported - which is what format-07753 is. Measured end to end: cache 12104 -> 12137, 33 blocks filled, dump folder emptied, no manual step. This is the gap that made a clean build look different from the maintainer one; it also covers new areas, which keep adding shaders as the player progresses. fill-cache refuses to guess at python: the Windows Store alias sits on PATH, does nothing and returns an error, so a candidate has to answer --version

run: prefill the cache before the first launch, so the first launch is complete. A fresh cache renders with gaps - the title screen is black - and until now that only healed on the second run. The launcher now runs the game headless for 25 seconds first, collects every block the cache lacks, translates them, and only then starts. Measured on a cache with 33 blocks removed: 12104 -> 12137 before the window opened, marker written, and the launch that followed reported 0 missing shaders. Once per cache; -noprefill skips it

gfx: log a lost device once, not once per frame. The retail log of one session with a lost device held 21,872 copies of the vkQueueSubmit2 line across 556 seconds - the game kept running (sound and logic are unaffected, so it reads as a hang when it is not) and every frame buried the frames that came BEFORE the loss, which are the ones that would say why it happened. Both submit paths now report once and say so. The submit itself is still attempted: stopping would change behaviour this change is not meant to touch. Verified: 25 s headless run, rendering, zero submit failures
